//! The memory adapter of the names port: the core's contract rows run through it, then the cases specific to it.

use super::adapter::NamesMemoryAdapter;
use crate::cases::{Case, Expect, Word, run};
use crate::outbound::names::errors::NamesError;
use crate::outbound::names::interface::NamesPort;
use crate::outbound::names::fixtures::contract::CASES as CONTRACT;
use crate::outbound::names::types::{Asked, Greeting};

type Input = Asked;
type Value = Greeting;
type Failure = NamesError;

/// The rows of this part's cases: a name, one case word, an input from the fixtures or a constructor, and the expected value or error variant.
const CASES: &[Case<Input, Value, Failure>] = &[
    Case {
        name: "memory greets the name the tests start from",
        word: Word::Succeeds,
        input: || Asked("Ada"),
        expect: Expect::Value(Greeting("hello, Ada")),
    },
    Case {
        name: "memory refuses a name written in another case",
        word: Word::Refuses,
        input: || Asked("ada"),
        expect: Expect::Error(NamesError::Missing),
    },
];

/// Calls the part on one input; the contract's rows and the adapter's own go through it.
fn subject(asked: Input) -> Result<Value, Failure> {
    NamesMemoryAdapter.stored(&asked)
}

#[test]
fn succeeds() {
    run(CONTRACT, Word::Succeeds, subject);
    run(CASES, Word::Succeeds, subject);
}

#[test]
fn refuses() {
    run(CONTRACT, Word::Refuses, subject);
    run(CASES, Word::Refuses, subject);
}

#[test]
fn fails() {
    run(CONTRACT, Word::Fails, subject);
}

#[test]
fn rejects() {
    run(CONTRACT, Word::Rejects, subject);
}
